---
title: "Self-check: Elimination and addition"
---

Answer each question before opening its explanation. Draw the relevant structure or step when asked; recognition alone can hide a charge or geometry error.

## 1. Can CH₃Br give an ordinary beta-elimination?

Draw the carbon skeleton before answering.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Check your answer"}
No. There is no beta carbon, and therefore no beta-H that could be removed to form an adjacent C=C bond.
:::

## 2. How many pair arrows describe E2?

Identify the source and destination of each.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Check your answer"}
Three: base lone pair to beta-H; C–H bond pair into the C–C pi bond; C–leaving-group pair onto the leaving group. These describe one concerted elementary step.
:::

## 3. What is anti-periplanar?

State the H–C–C–Br dihedral angle in the preferred simple anti arrangement.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Check your answer"}
180 degrees. The reacting C–H and C–Br bonds lie in one plane on opposite sides of the viewed C–C bond. A Newman drawing must specify front and rear bonds.
:::

## 4. Which alkenes follow formal elimination from 2-bromobutane?

List constitutional possibilities and note the E/Z case.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Check your answer"}
But-1-ene and but-2-ene. The latter can be E or Z; but-1-ene has two H atoms at its terminal alkene carbon and cannot have E/Z configurations.
:::

## 5. Why does ionic HBr addition favour 2-bromopropane from propene?

Assume no peroxides and use the supplied carbocation model.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Check your answer"}
Protonation giving a secondary carbocation is favoured over the alternative primary carbocation. Bromide then captures that intermediate, giving the observed connectivity in this model.
:::

## 6. Why is the Br₂ route a different drawing?

Name the key bridged intermediate and the relative opening geometry.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Check your answer"}
A bromonium intermediate can be opened by opposite-side bromide attack, giving anti addition. A free-carbocation HBr mechanism should not be copied unchanged for this process.
:::

If an answer was unexpected, return to the [worked practice](exercise.qmd), repair your own drawing and explain the change in a sentence.
